chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Humran said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pilgrim on the Day of Sacrifice: what is permissible for him? He said, 'Everything except women.' And about the Mutamatti' (one performing Tamattu' Hajj): what is permissible for him on the Day of Sacrifice? He said, 'Everything except women and perfume.' As for wearing clothes and covering the head, there is no objection to both after shaving the head and before the Tawaf (Visitation). The mention of this has already passed, and to add further clarification, he narrated:

key_terms.الزِّيَارَةِ: The Visitation (Tawaf al-Ziyarah of the Kaaba)

ai.seo_question: What is permissible for a pilgrim on the Day of Sacrifice after exiting Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific prohibitions (*mahdudat*) that lift upon the completion of the Hajj rites, distinguishing between the general permissibility of women for the *Hadi* pilgrim and the additional restriction on perfume for the *Mutamatti'* who must offer a sacrifice. It further refines the timeline for resuming normal attire, noting that wearing clothes and covering the head are permissible immediately after shaving the head, prior to performing *Tawaf al-Ziyarah*. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the precise sequence of ritual acts and their corresponding legal statuses.
